title: Resumable File Uploader
prompt: Design a reusable multi-file browser uploader supporting progress, pause, cancel and resume. The server issues upload sessions and presigned part URLs. Focus on memory bounds, retry correctness and what can actually survive a browser restart. Draw the component/data-flow architecture, define state owners and contracts, and explain performance, accessibility and recovery. No UI coding is required.
functionalReqs: Validate files and create per-file upload sessions
Upload bounded concurrent chunks with accurate progress
Resume incomplete sessions and clean up cancelled work
nonFunctionalReqs: Up to 2 GiB per file; three concurrent 8 MiB parts; no whole-file ArrayBuffer.
Provide a labelled file input as well as drag/drop, keyboard pause/cancel, text progress and throttled announcements. Validation errors identify the affected file.
Reconcile confirmed parts from server; retry the same part number/checksum safely. Expired sessions require explicit restart; cancel aborts active requests and informs the server.

scale.notes: Up to 2 GiB per file; three concurrent 8 MiB parts; no whole-file ArrayBuffer.
scale.storage: 3 active parts × 8 MiB; illustrative interview assumptions, not measured guarantees.

outOfScope: Backend sharding, ranking algorithms and infrastructure provisioning
Implementing a production UI inside this exercise
deepDives: Slice files into 8 MiB parts and upload at most three concurrently. Confirm progress only for acknowledged parts; in-flight bytes are provisional. Store session metadata in IndexedDB, not the whole file by default; after reload require re-selection and verify fingerprint unless a supported permissioned file handle is available.
A part succeeds but its acknowledgement times out
Whole-file upload is simpler for small files. Resumable multipart adds server coordination; persistent file access varies by browser and permission.
